subject.title: feat(openrouter): forward OpenClaw session id as session_id

question: Should OpenClaw support opt-in forwarding of a stable OpenRouter-scoped derived session identifier through the OpenRouter plugin, rather than keeping provider request identifiers entirely caller-configured?
rationale: The branch is mechanically narrow and avoids raw-ID disclosure, but deciding whether a stable session-correlating value may leave OpenClaw—and whether a dedicated plugin boolean is the enduring configuration contract—requires maintainer policy judgment.

options.title: Accept the scoped opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the dedicated default-off OpenRouter setting, require proof from the current hash-based head, and merge only after the external identifier-egress behavior is explicitly accepted.

options.title: Keep identifiers caller-controlled
options.body: Do not add the plugin setting and direct users to existing caller/provider request parameters until a broader request-context contract is designed.

options.title: Design a broader provider contract first
options.body: Pause this plugin-specific PR and decide whether a generic, reviewed session-context API should own this behavior across providers.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the dedicated default-off OpenRouter setting, require proof from the current hash-based head, and merge only after the external identifier-egress behavior is explicitly accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline explicitly routed the original product review to steipete, and the remaining blocker is a product/privacy contract choice rather than a mechanical code repair.
